quadrant_descriptions.hardened_caught_baseline_evaded: Adversarial perturbation successfully bypassed the unhardened baseline model (predicted Normal), but the adversarially hardened model correctly intercepted and classified the attack.
quadrant_descriptions.both_caught: The adversarial perturbation was insufficient to cross the decision boundary; both baseline and hardened models correctly detected the malicious intrusion.
quadrant_descriptions.both_failed: The adversarial perturbation was sufficiently aggressive to evade both models, causing both detectors to misclassify the attack as benign traffic.
quadrant_descriptions.baseline_caught_hardened_evaded: Investigated: 0 cases found out of 1,500 evaluated test samples. The hardened model was trained via multi-method adversarial data augmentation alongside clean traffic, expanding its robust decision boundary without degrading core intrusion boundaries. Under transfer attacks optimized against the baseline detector, no perturbation fooled the hardened model while leaving the baseline intact.

summary.investigation_notes: In 1,500 held-out test attack samples, 0 samples existed where only the baseline detected the attack. Adversarial hardening enriched the training manifold with FGSM, UAP, and DEMGAN perturbations without degrading benign or clean attack detection (clean FPR penalty: 0.0%). Under transfer attacks, perturbations designed to fool the baseline do not trick the hardened model while leaving the baseline intact.
summary.demgan_limitation_notice: DEMGAN in this project is an empirical manifold-drift surrogate approximation towards benign distribution centroids with calibrated stochastic jitter (Xu et al. 2025 surrogate), not an adversarial neural GAN generator with discriminator backpropagation.
summary.benchmark_simulation_notice: All adversarial evaluations are reproducible offline benchmark simulations based on mathematical perturbation vectors and domain invariant projections applied to held-out NSL-KDD test flows, not live network packet captures.
